source_caption:
The Florida Project (2017), directed by Sean Baker, introduced the world to one of the most unforgettable child performances in recent cinema. Brooklynn Prince was only six years old when she played Moonee, yet her performance felt incredibly real and emotional. She went on to win the Critics’ Choice Award for Best Young Performer and received many other nominations, quickly becoming the breakout star of the film. ￼

The story follows Moonee, a fearless and imaginative little girl living with her young mother in a cheap roadside motel just outside Disney World. To her, every day feels like an adventure, full of mischief, friendship, and small discoveries. But while the children see magic in their surroundings, the adults are quietly struggling to survive, trying to pay rent and avoid homelessness in a place that feels worlds away from the fantasy promised by nearby theme parks. ￼

What makes the film so powerful is the contrast between childhood innocence and harsh reality. Through Moonee’s eyes, the world still feels bright and playful, even as life around her becomes more unstable. The film doesn’t rely on big dramatic moments, instead it shows how poverty and survival unfold in everyday life.

At its heart, The Florida Project is about childhood, resilience, and imagination. It shows how kids can turn even the hardest situations into something that feels magical, while quietly reminding us that behind the laughter, there’s a much tougher story unfolding.

source_details.synopsis: The Florida Project is a 2017 American drama film directed by Sean Baker, written by Baker and Chris Bergoch, and starring Bria Vinaite in her film debut, Brooklynn Prince, and Willem Dafoe, with Valeria Cotto, Christopher Rivera, and Caleb Landry Jones in supporting roles. It was many of the cast members' first film appearance. The slice of life plot focuses on the summertime adventures of a six-year-old girl who lives with her unemployed single mother in a budget motel in Kissimmee, Florida. Their struggle to make ends meet and stave off homelessness takes place in a realistic environment near Walt Disney World, which was code-named "The Florida Project" during its planning stages.
